rule: PLAN.md section 9 says the MCP server is read-only by construction because it imports the query layer and not the append layer.
observed: mcp_server.py imports `chain`, the module defining Chain.append, alongside `query`.

because.quote: Read-only by construction: it imports the query layer, not the append layer.

why_ambiguous: PLAN.md does not define which module IS the append layer, and importing `chain` is not the same as calling `Chain.append`. The extractor author raised the same ambiguity unprompted and declined to take a position on it. Deciding this needs the owner, not another model.
why_no_packet: This never became a disagreement packet, and that is the interesting part. The `mcp` contract places no constraint on `facts.server_imports` at all, so the observation could not conflict with it and nothing was generated for the adjudicator to rule on. The same hole let fault mcp.4 -- which planted a fictional `gitio` import against the same sentence -- be ACCEPTED. A contract hole does not merely fail to catch a planted fault; it hides the real finding standing behind it.
found_via: chasing the six faults the contracts accepted, rather than by any check

grounding.checked_by: read directly from PLAN.md and mcp_server.py at the commit this was filed against
